Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Why p2:** Studio's Interfaces rail and the dashboard component list ignore the translation bundle on a zh-CN session, while the runtime sidebar on the same session translates.
- **Lane:** `domain:ui`. The landing is `previews/navItemLabel.ts`. Resolve through the same bundle reader the runtime sidebar uses.

Claim: PM loop round 2
Session: `session_01Vk15bz8xHtKGUfXfCm16h4`
Account: `os-elon-musk` (the seat's linked user as `GET /user` answers it; the card's assignee)
Branch: `claude/issue-12688-studio-rail-localized`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-12688`
Domain: `domain:ui`
Seat: `domain:ui#3`
File surface: `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, only the Interfaces pillar's nav rail (`studio-rail-interfaces`) and the dashboard property panel's component list, the DISPLAY text only; any child component or hook those two read in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` or `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/`. `navItemLabelText` in `previews/navItemLabel.ts` stays as it is, because the editors read it to echo the authored label. Tests beside each; one `.changeset/12688-*.md` (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (default tier; `dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui` over the named paths: no path-derived mandate)
Clause-②: no (display only; no export, prop or type changes)
Responsibility: `@object-ui/app-shell`'s Studio Interfaces pillar draws its nav rail and the dashboard component list from the code layer (`/layers`) through `navItemLabelText`, which reads only inline locale maps, so the server's `/meta` localization never reaches them | the runtime sidebar's path covers the runtime only: nav labels are localized at the server's `/meta` boundary (`translateApp`), the one owner `@object-ui/i18n`'s `navGroupLabel` docblock names | every author on a non-English session who opens Studio Interfaces, measured 2/2 and again 2/2 by QA (objectstack-ai/objectstack#23951); the reader the card names stands on `main` `2dbe5f5` (`navItemLabel.ts:40`, `StudioDesignSurface.tsx:4632`–`4633`)
Thread-read: 6218401597
Serial constraints cleared: objectui#12725 (`pm:queue`, not in flight, the Studio copilot's right slot) names `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and `StudioAiCopilot.tsx`: a different region and a different defect shape (gate ①), so serial, not fold. Whichever lands second merges `main`. No in-flight `domain:ui` claim and no open objectui PR names `studio-design/`, `previews/navItemLabel.ts` or `packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts`, read across the lane's `pm:dispatched` claims and all 7 open PRs' file lists 2026-10-16T18:23Z.

## Seat answer to the dev's open question · `domain:ui` seat 3 · `session_01Vk15bz8xHtKGUfXfCm16h4` · 2026-10-16T19:09Z

Report `6222758848`, open question 1: how the dashboard component list reaches the server's localized widget titles.

**Answer: A.** This is the seat's call, in its no-escalation class: the order and route of a technical task under governing text the dispatch already cited.
- **Governing text:** `@object-ui/i18n`'s `navGroupLabel` docblock. Localization of served documents is owned by the server's `/meta` boundary: "One owner, not two."
- The rail half of PR #12766 follows that text. B would put a second, client-side translator into the Studio chrome, and it overrides draft-edited titles unless it rebuilds A's guard. C leaves the card's own Expected line unmet.

**Shape of round 2** (the claim re-statement on this card widens the surface to carry it):
1. The component list in `DashboardDefaultInspector.tsx` DRAWS a widget's served title only while the draft widget's title equals the published layer's, matched by widget `id`. The rule is the rail's (`servedNavText.ts`), reused or mirrored for widgets. A widget changed or added in the draft shows its authored title.
2. The served text comes from what the server already answers localized for this request: the `/meta/dashboard` list the console's `MetadataProvider` holds, or the pillar's own `/meta` read if that is the one in hand. ⛔ No `useObjectLabel().widgetTitle` and no bundle key is built.
3. It reaches the inspector through an app-shell-internal channel. No exported prop, type or context is added, so `Clause-②: no` stands.
4. Every editor input keeps the authored title.
5. The canvas's own client-bundle pass (`DashboardPreview` without `localized`) is not this round's: it is the PR's acceptance note, not a change here.

When both halves are on the branch, the PR body's first line becomes `Fixes #12688`.

### Replacement PR body for #12766, for the seat to write

The os-dev contract keeps a dev off a PR body after `pr_create`, so this run did not send the budgeted update. The replacement body follows verbatim. Line 1 is the closing keyword for this card.

```markdown
Fixes #12688
Clause-②: no

## What

On a zh-CN session the Studio drew two surfaces in the authored English, while the runtime on the same session drew the translated text:

- the **Interfaces rail** (heading, group headings and rows);
- the dashboard property panel's **component list**.

This PR fixes both. Both now draw what the server's `/meta` boundary already localized. Every editor keeps the authored text.

## Mechanism (measured on a real console)

- **Rail.** The rail drew the nav editor's buffer: the app's pending draft, else `GET /api/v1/meta/app/showcase_app/layers`, the authored code layer. On zh-CN that read answers `Capability Map`. The pillar's app load already sends `GET /api/v1/meta/app?package=com.example.showcase` with the session's `Accept-Language`, and the server answers it through `translateApp`: 功能展示, and 能力地图 / 页面搭建 / 工作区 / 数据模型 / 图表画廊.
- **Component list.** The list drew the dashboard leaf's buffer: its draft, else `GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/showcase_chart_gallery/layers`, which answers `Task Count vs Avg Progress`. The console's metadata store already holds `GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard`, and the server answers it through `translateDashboard`: 任务数与平均进度 for `combo_count_vs_progress`.
- **Canvas.** The dashboard canvas's 任务数与平均进度 comes from neither read. `DashboardPreview` mounts `DashboardRenderer` without `localized`, so the renderer translates through the client bundle. That pass is unchanged here; see the acceptance notes.

## Fix

**One rule, two surfaces.** The served text is drawn for an entry or widget whose authored text in the buffer equals its text in the published layer. Entries are matched by nav entry `id`, widgets by widget `id`. An entry or widget changed or added in the draft draws its authored text, as before. Both surfaces use one comparison, `sameLabel` in `servedNavText.ts`.

- **Rail: `studio-design/servedNavText.ts`.** It pairs the served app row with the `/layers` effective layer. The rail's rows, group headings and heading draw the resulting display tree. The leaf opened on load is resolved from the same tree, so its caption matches its row.
- **Component list: `studio-design/servedDashboardText.ts`.** It pairs the served dashboard from the metadata store with the published layer.
  - With no pending draft, the published layer is the baseline the leaf load already read.
  - With a pending draft, the pillar reads `/layers` once. It does so only for a dashboard the server serves, so a never-published draft still asks no `/layers` (objectui#11799).
  - The pillar hands the pairing to `DashboardDefaultInspector` through one app-shell-internal context, `ServedWidgetTextContext`. It is not exported from the package root, and no prop or type changes. Outside the Studio pillar the context is empty, and the list reads as it always has.

Every editor keeps reading the authored buffer:

- the nav editor's cards (`AppNavCanvas`);
- the nav-item inspector's Label input and the nav inspector's head;
- a source page's list of nav entries;
- the widget inspector's Title input;
- the canvas's rename strip;
- the component list's selection labels.

There is no second translator: no key is built and no client bundle is read, which follows the `navGroupLabel` docblock in `@object-ui/i18n` ("One owner, not two").

## Acceptance notes

- **Canvas, unchanged here.** The Studio dashboard canvas (`DashboardPreview`, `DashboardRenderer` without `localized`) translates widget titles through the client bundle, and that pass also runs over a draft. A widget title edited in a draft would therefore draw as the packaged translation on the canvas, while the component list now draws the authored edit. This is a read-only observation, not measured live. Carrier: none.
- **App navigation has no explicit-override rule.** `translateApp` in `@objectstack/spec` applies the bundle by nav id whatever the published label is, while `translateDashboard` follows "The catalog LOSES to an explicit override". A nav label edited and published over a packaged translation would therefore still be served, and drawn by the runtime sidebar and this rail, as the bundle's text. This is a read-only observation, not measured live. Carrier: none.
- **Stale list right after a publish.** The served dashboard list is the metadata store's. A publish triggers that store's refresh (`emitMetadataRefresh`). Until the refresh lands, a widget whose new published title still equals the buffer's would draw the store's previous served title. Not measured.
- **Editor pins are vitest only.** The showcase package is read-only on this backend: the rail offers no Edit toggle there, and the component list offers no remove or drag. The editor pins are measured in the vitest harness only.
- **Backend build artifact.** To boot the card's example, the verify backend checkout needed `packages/connectors/connector-slack` built. Its `dist` was absent, and the showcase config failed to compile without it. That was a build artifact only; no tracked file changed.
```
